wu: Students play 'Simon Says' with morning actions: 'Simon says wake up!', 'Simon says brush your teeth!', 'Simon says wash your face!', 'Simon says eat breakfast!', 'Simon says go to school!'. They perform the actions and shout the verbs.
wuAlt: Students do a 'Morning Routine Relay' in teams: run to the board, point to a flashcard of 'wake up', run back, high-five next student who points to 'wash', etc.
Students play 'What's Missing?': I show 5 flashcards (wake up, wash, brush teeth, eat, go to school), they close eyes, I remove one, they guess 'What is missing? It is __.'
pres: I show a big poster of a boy's morning routine with 5 pictures in random order. I model: 'First, I wake up. Then, I wash my face. Next, I brush my teeth. Then, I eat breakfast. Finally, I go to school.' I ask 'What is first?' and students point to the picture. I check understanding with 'What do I do after wake up?'
presAlt: I use a storybook 'My Busy Morning' with repeating sentences: 'I wake up. I wash. I eat. I go to school.' I pause and ask 'What is next?'
I act out the routine with props: a pillow (wake up), a towel (wash), a toothbrush (brush teeth), a banana (eat), a bag (go to school). Students say the verbs as I act.
prac: Students work in pairs with a cut-and-stick worksheet of 5 morning actions. They cut out the pictures and glue them in order on a timeline strip. They practice saying: 'First, I __. Then, I __. Next, I __.' I help with pronunciation and sentence structure.
pracAlt: Students play 'Routine Order Race' in teams: I give each group a set of 5 picture cards. They race to put them in order and say the sequence correctly.
Students play 'Teacher Says': I say a sequence like 'First, wake up. Then, wash.' and students mime it in order.
ls: Students listen to an audio of a girl describing her morning routine. They have 5 picture cards and put them in the order they hear. I play the audio twice: 'I wake up at 7. Then, I wash my face. Next, I brush my teeth. Then, I eat bread. Finally, I go to school.'
re: Students play 'Morning Routine Freeze Dance': I play music, they dance/mime morning actions. When I pause, they freeze and I ask 'What are you doing?' They answer 'I am __.' (e.g., 'I am brushing my teeth.')
prod: Students draw their own morning routine in 3 steps on a paper strip. They present to a partner: 'First, I __. Then, I __. Next, I __.' I encourage them to use the sequence words and add details like 'I eat bread' or 'I drink milk'.
rw: Students trace 3 simple sentences: 'I wake up. I wash. I eat.' Then they copy the sentences under the pictures. For fast finishers, they write their own 3-step routine: 'First, __. Then, __. Next, __.'
st: We sing the 'Good Morning Song' with actions: 'Good morning, good morning, wake up! Good morning, good morning, wash your face! Good morning, good morning, eat your bread! Good morning, good morning, go to school!' Then we do the goodbye routine: Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Students have bingo cards with morning actions. I call out 'Wake up!' and they cover the picture. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Teams race to put 5 picture cards in order on the board and say the sequence correctly.
I show 3 picture cards in order. Students close eyes, I swap two, they guess what changed.
Students mime a morning action, others guess 'Are you __?' (e.g., 'Are you brushing your teeth?')
Students sit in a circle. Student 1 says 'First, I wake up.' Student 2 says 'First, I wake up. Then, I wash.' and so on.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: They write a 4-step morning routine and draw a picture for each step.
Support / weaker learners: They use a sentence frame with picture cues: 'First, I __. Then, I __. Next, I __.'
hw: Read your morning routines mini-book to someone at home. Point to the pictures and say the sentences.
Draw your family's morning routine and label 3 actions in English.
Play 'Teacher Says' with your family using morning actions.
tip: Use the local context: ask students what they eat for breakfast (e.g., 'Do you eat bread and milk?') to make the routine personal and relevant to Moroccan culture.
